newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean yields end higher on liquidity concerns.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean yields end higher on liquidity concerns.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds closed higher on Tuesday due to persistent concerns about tight liquidity towards the month end, dealers said.
Active individual buying of certificates of deposits pushed the three-month yield to a higher close.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.52 against Monday's 12.49 * 3-mth CDs end at 15.70 against 15.50 * Overnight average unchanged at 17.0 -----------------------------------------------------------
But the Daewoo Securities dealer said corporate money demand ahead of Chusok (the Korean Thanksgiving holidays) would push the three-year yields to a 12.50-12.70 boxed range.
"I cannot rule out the possibility of the corporate bond hitting a new year high of 12.70 before Chusok," he added.
Recently sharply rising yields on commercial papers (CP) also contributed to CD yields rising further.

The central bank extended the maturity of half of 1.6 trillion won worth of Repos by four days. Dealers said this helped the market ease tight liquidity concerns. The Repo was matured on Tuesday. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
